subject: Situation room summary — Quantiva Labs API latency spike
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: [SITROOM] Quantiva API latency spike (SEV-2)

Team —

Observed a sustained latency spike impacting Quantiva Labs (prod-us) starting ~09:05 PT. Error rates are low (~0.3%), but p95/p99 token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s and requests are timing out for long-context jobs. Affected model: rdl-7b-v2 (hosted).

What we've done so far:
- Rolled back a recent kernel selector change on a small subset of hosts (did not fully restore).
- Temporarily routed Quantiva traffic to standby pool (partial relief; tail latency improved but throughput constrained).
- Collected perf traces and KV cache metrics (attached: situation-room-log-20260822.txt).

Immediate asks:
- Markus: decide whether we escalate to a public exec update and offer Quantiva an on-call exec bridge.
- Mina: continue tracing kernel selection path + validate quantization fallback.
- Michael: confirm capacity to scale standby pool further and estimate ETA.

I'll keep incremental logs in the sitroom folder (link in thread). Planning to open a Zoom bridge in 5 minutes.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: situation-room-log-20260822.txt

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@quantiva.com>, Quantiva Ops <ops@quantiva.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Executive update: temporary service degradation (Quantiva Labs) — 09:22 PT

Sarah / Quantiva team —

I’m Markus, Head of Customer Solutions at Redwood. Ben flagged a latency spike affecting a subset of Quantiva production traffic beginning at ~09:05 PT this morning. We classify this as SEV-2: user-facing tail latency increases with partial request timeouts for long-context jobs.

Current status (09:22 PT):
- Impact: elevated tail latency for a subset (~6%) of requests routed to rdl-7b-v2. Core generation functions remain available for most shorter contexts.
- Mitigation: We have temporarily routed your traffic to a standby pool which has reduced p99 latency for many requests. We are continuing to scale capacity while engineering traces the root cause.
- Next update: 10:00 PT or earlier if we have substantive changes.

Short-term commitments:
- We will provide a dedicated postmortem and timeline within 48 hours.
- We will offer a good-faith credit for impacted tokens if the final postmortem indicates regression on our side.
- A technical owner will be on a call until resolved — join via the sitroom link if you’d like (see drive link).

Attachments: executive-update-slide.pdf (one-pager showing current traffic split and interim mitigations).

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. Ben and our on-call infra team are actively working this and I’ll provide the next update at 10:00 PT. If you need more frequent touchpoints, reply here and we’ll escalate to an exec audio bridge.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0183

1) Can you confirm whether any user data was retried or reprocessed as part of the routing change? We need to understand potential duplication for compliance.

3) We will probably request a formal SLA credit if this impacts more than 2% of delivered tokens in our weekly window — please include guidance on next steps.

We will join the sitroom. Please ping when the bridge is live.

—Sarah

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident next steps and immediate RCA summary — Quantiva Labs (SEV-2, resolved)

Sarah / Quantiva team —

Post-incident update (12:30 PT): the engineering team identified a regressor in our kernel-choice heuristic that, under certain sequence-length distributions, incorrectly preferred an execution path with suboptimal cache locality. That produced increased stalls at the tail when workloads had long contexts and heterogeneous tokenization. We reverted the selector globally at 11:05 PT and continued scaling standby capacity; metrics show p99 latency returned to baseline by ~11:40 PT.

Direct answers to your asks:
1) Data duplication: the routing change did not retry or reprocess payloads. We routed live traffic to a different pool; requests that timed out were client-visible timeouts — we have logs of request ids and will share a list on the secure drive for your reconciliation.
2) Suspected cause: the regression was introduced in a kernel selector change deployed in a staged rollout last week. The selector favors a quantization path that can increase KV cache churn for long-context sequences; under the distribution of Quantiva's recent workload, that manifested as increased tail stalls.
3) SLA credits: we will evaluate the token impact over your weekly window and follow the SLA process. I will assign a Customer Success rep to coordinate the credit calculation and next steps.

Next steps and timeline:
- 48h: full postmortem document and timeline to be delivered (includes diagnosis, impact table, and remediation plan).
- 72h: production test plan for a conservative kernel-selection update with additional heuristics; we will share test harness results with your team.
- Ongoing: weekly sync until your long-context workloads show stable p99s below the agreed SLO.

Attachments: postmortem-agenda.docx (proposed structure for the 48h postmortem + 72h remediation milestones).

If you prefer, we can set a short exec call this afternoon to walk through the postmortem outline. We appreciate your patience and will own the follow-through.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
